paper.title: When Can We Track Significant Preference Shifts in Dueling Bandits?

settings.name_in_paper: Switching dueling bandits under SST∩STI with significant CW switches
unmapped: Preferences also satisfy the stochastic triangle inequality (STI) w.r.t. a per-round total ordering
Non-stationarity measured by the number L_sig of significant Condorcet winner switches (unknown to learner); preference matrix may change every round
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t$, there exists a total ordering on arms, denoted by $\succ_t$, and $\forall i\succeq_t j\succeq_t k$: (a) $\delta_t(i,k) \geq \max\{\delta_t(i,j),\delta_t(j,k)\}$ (SST). (b) ... (STI).

settings.name_in_paper: Switching dueling bandits under the Condorcet winner condition (lower bound)
unmapped: Preference matrix may change every round (here drawn i.i.d. from a mixture by an oblivious adversary) while the number of significant CW switches is 0
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t$, there is a {\bf Condorcet winner} arm, denoted by $a_t^*$, such that $\delta_t(a_t^*,a) \geq 0$ for all $a\in[K]\bs\{a_t^*\}$.

unmapped: Preference matrix may change every round while the number of significant CW switches is 0; STI not assumed
settings.definition_quote: there exists a finite family $\mc{F}$ of switching dueling bandit environments with $K=3$ that satisfies the SST condition with $\Lsig=0$ significant shifts.

algorithms.name: METASWIFT (Meta-Elimination while Tracking Arms in SWIFT)

symbols.phase_len: length tau_{i+1}-tau_i of the i-th significant phase

conditions: SST and STI hold at every round (Definition 2)
tuning: eviction/switching threshold constant C > 0 large enough

source.label: thm:metaswift
source.quote: Suppose SST and STI hold (see \Cref{assumption:sst+sti}). Let $\{\tau_i\}_{i=0}^{\Lsig}$ denote the unknown significant shifts of \Cref{definition:sig-shift}. Then, for some constant $C_0>0$, \Cref{meta-alg} has expected dynamic regret \[ \mb{E}[\DR(T)] \leq C_0\log^3(T)\sum_{i=0}^{\Lsig} \sqrt{K\cdot (\tau_{i+1}-\tau_i)}, \]

results.notes: Dynamic regret against per-round Condorcet winner, defined via preference gaps (expectation). Algorithm does not know L_sig or shift times; takes horizon T as input.

symbols.L_sig: number of significant Condorcet winner switches in T rounds (unknown to learner)

conditions: SST and STI hold at every round (Definition 2)
tuning: eviction/switching threshold constant C > 0 large enough

source.label: thm:metaswift
source.quote: and using Jensen's inequality, this implies a regret rate of $C_0\log^3(T)\sqrt{K\cdot (\Lsig+1)\cdot T}$.

symbols.V_CW: Condorcet winner variation sum_{t=2}^T max_a |P_t(a_t^*,a)-P_{t-1}(a_t^*,a)| (unknown to learner)

conditions: SST and STI hold at every round (Definition 2)

source.label: cor:tv
source.quote: Let $V_T := \sum_{t=2}^T \max_{a\in [K]} |P_t(a_t^*,a)-P_{t-1}(a_t^*,a)|$ be the unknown Condorcet winner variation. Using the same notation of \Cref{thm:metaswift}: \Cref{meta-alg} has expected dynamic regret \[ \mb{E}[\DR(T)] \leq C_0\log^{3}(T) \left(\sqrt{KT} + (KV_T)^{1/3} T^{2/3}\right). \]

results.notes: Paper's V_T is a CW variation, not the canonical total-variation budget; declared as V_CW.

conditions: Condorcet winner condition holds every round

source.label: thm:lower-bound
source.quote: For each horizon $T$, there exists a finite family $\mc{F}$ of switching dueling bandit environments with $K=3$ that satisfies the Condorcet winner condition (\Cref{assumption:winner}) with $\Lsig=0$ significant shifts. The worst-case regret of any algorithm on an environment $\mc{E}$ in this family is lower bounded as \[ \sup_{\mc{E}\in\mc{F}} \mb{E}_{\mc{E}} \left[ \DR(T) \right] \geq T/8. \]

results.notes: Linear regret despite zero significant shifts; construction uses L = Omega(T) changes.

source.label: cor:lower-bound
source.quote: For each horizon $T$, there exists a finite family $\mc{F}$ of switching dueling bandit environments with $K=3$ that satisfies the SST condition with $\Lsig=0$ significant shifts. The worst-case regret of any algorithm on an environment $\mc{E}$ in this family is lower bounded as \[ \sup_{\mc{E}\in\mc{F}} \mb{E}_{\mc{E}} \left[ \DR(T) \right] \geq T/8. \]

results.notes: Same construction as Theorem 3, which satisfies SST but violates STI.

source.label: cor:lower-bound
source.quote: For each horizon $T$, there exists a finite family $\mc{F}$ of switching dueling bandit environments with $K=3$ that satisfies the STI condition with $\Lsig=0$ significant shifts. The worst-case regret of any algorithm on an environment $\mc{E}$ in this family is lower bounded as \[ \sup_{\mc{E}\in\mc{F}} \mb{E}_{\mc{E}} \left[ \DR(T) \right] \geq T/8. \]

results.notes: Uses construction of Remark 2; label duplicated with Corollary 9 in source. Proof details only sketched.
